tech_stack: C#, ASP.NET Core (.NET), SQL Server (multi-tenant regional DBs), Kafka (Avro schema), Redis (cache), Azure Blob Storage

http_deps: ProfileService — publish target profiles and SBP profiles
FMSClientManager — file management system blob operations
HtmlHostServiceClient — HTML site hosting and access URLs
background_services: ExpirationBackgroundService — polls regional DBs for expired content items and processes them
CustomPropertyBackgroundService — propagates custom property schema changes to content
ScheduleActivateBackgroundService — activates content versions on their scheduled date
ScheduleAddToProfileBackgroundService — adds content to publish profiles on schedule
ECMMigrationBackgoundService — migrates Enterprise Content Management data into CMS
SystemStateBackgroundService — monitors and updates content system availability state
SyncIndicatorBGService — dequeues sync indicator messages and triggers external sync
CustomPropertyEventListener — consumes CMS custom property Kafka events
AugmentationEventListener — consumes static augmentation pipeline events
VirusScanEventListener — processes blob virus scan results and updates file status
CrackingPipelineMetaEventListener — handles CCP (content cracking pipeline) metadata events
VFSEventListener — handles video file system processed events
ExpirationNotificationSettingListener — handles expiration notification setting changes
DebouncedEventProcessorService — debounces and batches content events before downstream emission

domains.name: File & Versioning
domains.responsibility: Manages the full lifecycle of library content items and their versions, including creation, checkout/checkin, activation, shortcuts, and format-specific types (articles, freestyle, live docs, static resources).
domains.health_reason: FileManager contains only GetFile(); FileVersionManager contains only GetFileVersion() and GetLatestFileVersion(); ItemManager contains only GetItemTeamSites(). All real business logic (add, copy, move, delete, checkout, activate) resides in Express static Writer classes at the application layer.

invariants: A file must belong to exactly one TeamSite
A checked-out file may only be modified by the user who checked it out
OriginItemId resolves to OriginLink when OriginType == SHORTCUT
IsLatestAll and IsLatestApproved flags must be consistent across versions
MajorVersionNumber.MinorVersionNumber must be monotonically increasing per file

domains.name: Folder
domains.responsibility: Manages the hierarchical folder structure within a TeamSite library, including creation, renaming, moving, copying, and deletion of folders.
domains.health_reason: No FolderManager exists; only FolderRepository provides data access. All folder action logic (move, copy, delete) lives in Express Writer classes (CopyFolderCommon, DeleteFolderCommon). No domain invariants are enforced at the aggregate level.

invariants: A folder must have a valid ParentId within the same TeamSite
LibraryMaterializedPath must be a slash-delimited chain of ancestor folder IDs
Deleting a folder cascades to all child items and sub-folders

domains.name: Publishing & Distribution
domains.responsibility: Controls publication of content versions to distribution profiles (SBP profiles), including scheduled publishing, promotion of versions, and publish status tracking.
domains.health_reason: No dedicated PublishingManager or PublishAggregate exists; all publish logic is in Express Reader/Writer static methods (PublishReader, FileWriter publish paths). PublishController and SchedulePublishController delegate entirely to Express layer with no domain object enforcing publish rules.

invariants: Only the latest approved version may be published to a profile
A file cannot be published if it is in CheckedOut status
Scheduled publish date must be in the future

domains.name: TeamSite
domains.responsibility: Manages workspace containers (TeamSites) and their memberships; TeamSites are the top-level organizational unit that scopes content, permissions, and custom properties.
domains.health_reason: TeamSiteMemberManager.GetTeamSiteMembers() exists but is thin. TeamSite CRUD operations and member management are mostly read-only lookups. No domain rules enforced for membership changes or TeamSite lifecycle in the domain layer.

invariants: A TeamSite must have at least one owner/admin member
Content within a TeamSite is scoped to that workspace for permission resolution

domains.name: Content Permission
domains.responsibility: Controls access rights to content items and TeamSites, including role-based and granular unique permissions, and content sharing with external or internal users.
domains.health_reason: ContentPermissionManager.GetPermissions() and GetFullControlMembers() exist but contain only queries. Business rules for permission assignment and enforcement live in Express Writer classes. The FakeMode static flag is an infrastructure/testing concern leaked into the domain class.

invariants: Unique permissions override inherited TeamSite permissions
Full-control members can modify any permission
Content sharing must not grant permissions exceeding the granting user's own access level

domains.name: Custom Property
domains.responsibility: Defines the custom metadata schema for a TeamSite and manages the values of those properties on content items, supporting content tagging, filtering, and search enrichment.
domains.health_reason: CustomPropertyManager only has GetCustomPropertyType(). All bulk update and assignment logic lives in Express writers and background services (CustomPropertyBackgroundService). Custom property values are stored as raw XML blobs inside ItemModel.CustomPropertyXml rather than as typed value objects.

invariants: A custom property value must match its definition's allowed types/values
Hidden properties are not exposed through standard API responses
Custom property changes must be propagated to all content items in scope via background job

domains.name: External Sync
domains.responsibility: Manages bidirectional synchronization of content between the CMS and external systems (Google Drive, OneDrive, other ECM systems), including connection state, sync configuration, and cloud content ingestion.
domains.health_reason: ExternalSyncManager has UpdateConnectionStateAsync() and GetConnectionSyncConfigIdsAsync(), and ExternalContentSynchronizationTaskV2Manager exists. However, the complex sync orchestration logic (add/update external file versions) lives in Express Writer static methods rather than domain aggregates.

invariants: A sync config must reference a valid external connection
Disabled sync configs must not trigger sync jobs
Auto-publish flag determines whether synced content is automatically published on sync

domains.name: Workflow
domains.responsibility: Proxies content version submission to and from an external Workflow Service for approval-based publishing, tracking review status and controlling which versions may be promoted.
domains.health_reason: WorkflowRequestProxy is a pure HTTP proxy with no domain logic. ReviewController delegates entirely to Express Reader. No workflow aggregate, invariants, or domain events are modeled in this service; the Workflow Service is external.

invariants: A version may not be published if its WorkflowStatus is PendingReview
Only approved versions may be activated
Rejection returns the version to Draft state

domains.name: Content Query
domains.responsibility: Provides flexible, multi-dimensional querying and search across content items by metadata, custom properties, folder paths, TeamSite membership, and AI-assisted relevance.
domains.health_reason: No QueryManager or query aggregate exists in the domain layer. All query logic lives in Express Reader static classes (FlexibleContentQueryReader, ContentQueryReader, AIMLReader). Content relationships (RelationshipController) and URL generation (UrlController) are co-located here without domain encapsulation.

invariants: Query results must be filtered to content the requesting user has at least view permission on
AI-suggested queries must fall back to standard query on model unavailability

domains.name: Activity & Analytics
domains.responsibility: Records and retrieves user interaction events with content (views, downloads, shares) and aggregates them into live insights reports and data collection streams for analytics consumers.
domains.health_reason: LiveInsightsReportManager and LiveInsightsReportService exist but contain only data retrieval. Activity recording logic lives in Express ActivityWriter. DataCollectionController and AutomationController have no corresponding domain objects.

invariants: Activity events must reference a valid content item
Anonymous views must not include personally identifiable user data

domains.name: Content Expiration
domains.responsibility: Manages expiration policies on content items, triggers automated expiration processing (unpublish, notification) based on configured dates, and handles expiration notification settings.
domains.health_reason: ExpirationBackgroundService and ExpirationJobExecutor exist with real processing logic including multi-tenant iteration, notification, and content expiry. However, the domain aggregate for expiration policy is not explicitly modeled; expiration date is a field on ItemModel rather than a separate ExpirationPolicy aggregate.

invariants: Expiration date must be in the future when set
Expired content must be unpublished from all profiles
Expiration notification must fire before the expiration date based on configured lead time

domains.name: Content Collaboration
domains.responsibility: Enables user engagement on content through comments, document annotations, expert designations, and notifications related to content events.
domains.health_reason: No collaboration domain objects exist; CommentWriter, AnnotationWriter, AskExpertWriter, ExpertWriter are all Express-layer static classes. No comment or annotation aggregate is modeled in the domain layer.

invariants: Annotations are scoped to a specific content version
Only the annotation author or a full-control member may delete an annotation

domains.name: MicroApp
domains.responsibility: Manages interactive embedded application content (Tiled micro-apps) that can be created, edited, and embedded within the content library as a special content type.
domains.health_reason: MicroAppManager and MicroAppRepository exist. TiledClient handles external Tiled API integration. However, business rules for MicroApp lifecycle are thin and the ExtensiveFileWriter performs the actual domain orchestration.

invariants: A MicroApp must have a valid Tiled workspace ID
Only one user may edit a MicroApp at a time (edit lock)

domains.name: Content Rendering
domains.responsibility: Manages how content is rendered and viewed, including PDF/image renditions, HTML site hosting, content view configurations, and universal player metadata for different content formats.
domains.health_reason: RenditionHttpClient is a thin HTTP client with no domain logic. ContentView operations live in Express ContentViewReader/Writer. No rendering aggregate or domain rules exist; this domain is a thin proxy to external rendering services.

invariants: Renditions are version-scoped and must be invalidated when a new version is activated
HTML site access URLs must be regenerated after content updates

domains.name: System Operations
domains.responsibility: Encompasses system-level operations including feature flag management, background job control, admin tooling, system state monitoring, system identity resolution, and AI/ML-assisted content operations.
domains.health_reason: AppConfigurationManager exists with GetContentManagerAppSetting() and GetBlockedFileExtensions() but all other operations (feature toggles, background job management, system state) are thin controllers delegating to infrastructure. No system aggregate enforces invariants.

invariants: Blocked file extensions must be enforced at file upload time
Feature flags must be evaluated per-tenant using LaunchDarkly

steps.label: Validate file extension against blocked list (AppConfiguration)
Persist file record and initial version (FileRepository)
Validate file is in Active/approved state
Check version is not checked out
Update publish status on content record
Fetch external content from provider (GoogleContentSyncClient / OneDriveContentSyncClient)
Create or update file and version record
Apply metadata mapping to custom properties
ExpirationBackgroundService polls regional DBs for items past ExpirationDate
ContentExpireProcessor unpublishes content from all profiles
Author submits version for review (WorkflowRequestProxy → external Workflow Service)
Reviewer approves or rejects via ReviewController
Approval callback updates WorkflowStatus on version
Approved version becomes eligible for activation and publish

gap_analysis.title: Anemic domain layer — business logic in static Express Writers
gap_analysis.detail: FileManager has only GetFile(). FileVersionManager has only GetFileVersion() and GetLatestFileVersion(). ItemManager has only GetItemTeamSites(). All real business logic (add, copy, move, delete, checkout, activate, publish) lives in static application-layer Writer classes (AddFileCommon, CopyFileCommon, DeleteFileCommon, ActivationWriter, etc.). Domain aggregates enforce no invariants and emit no domain events.

gap_analysis.title: Cross-aggregate repository access in FileVersionManager
gap_analysis.detail: FileVersionManager depends on IFileRepository (not IFileVersionRepository) to retrieve versions. FileVersions should be accessed through the File aggregate root or a dedicated FileVersionRepository, not by bypassing aggregate boundaries with the parent's repository.

gap_analysis.title: Custom property values stored as XML strings in aggregate root
gap_analysis.detail: ItemModel.CustomPropertyXml is a raw XML string containing all property values. Parsing logic (GetCustomPropertyIdNameValueDict, CustomPropertyTextSearch, CustomPropertyAzureSearch) is embedded directly in the entity, creating a hidden value object that should be a proper typed class. This also makes property access O(n) parse operations.

gap_analysis.title: FakeMode static flag leaks testing concern into domain classes
gap_analysis.detail: ContentPermissionManager and TeamSiteMemberManager both expose `public static bool FakeMode` which, when set, redirects calls through ServiceCollectionHelper.GetScopedService (service locator anti-pattern). Infrastructure/testing concerns should not exist in domain classes.

gap_analysis.title: Missing domain events — state transitions emit Kafka events directly from application layer
gap_analysis.detail: No explicit domain event types model state transitions (ContentPublishedEvent, VersionActivatedEvent, ContentExpiredEvent). Kafka messages are produced directly in Express Writer static methods via SearchProducer without routing through domain aggregate events. This bypasses domain boundary enforcement.

gap_analysis.title: ItemModel represents both files and folders via IsFolder flag
gap_analysis.detail: ItemModel has an IsFolder property that switches its meaning. Files and folders are distinct concepts with different lifecycles and invariants but share one entity class. This inflates the aggregate and makes type-specific invariant enforcement impossible without if/else branching.

gap_analysis.title: WorkflowRequestProxy is a pure HTTP proxy with no domain logic
gap_analysis.detail: WorkflowRequestProxy contains only HTTP forwarding with no domain invariants (e.g., preventing publish of pending-review versions should be enforced here). Workflow state impacts File & Versioning lifecycle but no guard exists at the domain boundary.

gap_analysis.title: ExpirationPolicy is not a first-class aggregate
gap_analysis.detail: Expiration date is stored as a nullable field on ItemModel (ExpirationDate) rather than as a separate ExpirationPolicy aggregate. ExpirationBackgroundService iterates raw DB queries instead of loading domain aggregates. Expiration business rules (notification lead time, auto-unpublish) are scattered across ExpirationJobExecutor, ContentExpireProcessor, and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor.

gap_analysis.title: Content Rendering has no domain representation — thin proxy only
gap_analysis.detail: RenditionHttpClient, ContentViewReader, and ContentViewWriter are purely infrastructure/application-layer components with no domain aggregate for rendition state. Rendition lifecycle (Pending → Processing → Ready → Failed) is not modeled, making it impossible to enforce that a content item may not be published without a ready rendition.
